results.reason: The status task's own behaviour is the implementation's design. SPEC.md 8.6 says only that expects names a task by which the producer can learn the outcome; that a query of a held ceremony is answered with a response of the task's own type, without recording an approval or running the effect, is the minimal reading of that and not stated text. Not gating. (observed: pass)

Profile rule, not specification text: nothing normative says the relationship DID must differ from the connection DID (docs/07 O26; relationship DIDs unique per VRC is the user's decision, stricter than the specifications). Not gating. (observed: pass)
Per-VRC uniqueness is stricter than the specifications' per-relationship wording (docs/07 O26, O21); the specifications do not forbid reuse with the same counterparty. Not gating. (observed: pass)
The credential specification forbids using a pairwise identifier with a second counterparty; what the propose receiver must do on seeing one is not stated (docs/07 O26). Not gating. (observed: pass)

The specification says the receipt carries the computed digest but not whether a request digest that disagrees is refused or ignored; the vector accepts only the ignore reading (design docs/04 section 11). Not gating. (observed: pass)

Whether a redelivery of an existing credential under a new envelope is a refusal (framework 'creating something') or an idempotent receipt (design) is unsettled (docs/07 O21); the vector asserts the design reading (one stored credential, same digest). Not gating. (observed: pass)
Second VRC for one exchange: the specifications say nothing; the plan refuses with issue:alreadyIssued (docs/07 O21). Not gating. (observed: pass)

Whether a second VRC for the same connection pair is allowed at all is open (docs/07 O21); docs/07 section 1 (unique per VRC) makes it a new exchange with a new relationship DID. Not gating. (observed: pass)
Which key and verification relationship sign a VRC's inner proof is not stated normatively (the credential specification's examples use assertionMethod; docs/07 O17). Not gating. (observed: pass)

The specification asks for idempotent recording but also says a request that was already decided is noPending; which answer a repeat after the commit gets is not stated. The vector asserts the repeated answer and no second effect. Not gating. (observed: fail)

A device refuses to prompt when it is not a member of the named approverSet (consumer 6); the harness cannot know a set the device belongs to, so whether this request is prompted depends on the implementation's own enrolment. Not gating. (observed: pass)
The specification says the device refuses to prompt and names `expired`, and also allows a response with status refused; which of the two is the refusal is not stated. Not gating. (observed: fail)
failures: step 2: expected code expired, got taskFailed

results.reason: A decision that leaves the threshold unmet is answered with the specification's `pending` status or, equally, with a trust-task-next-step hold (the framework's own vocabulary for a held task; the hold rule of 8.6 is checked); the two differ in form only. Which one an implementation uses is not asserted. Not gating. (observed: pass)
The specification does not say whether a second delivery of a credential already held is stored again. The vector asserts one copy. Not gating. (observed: pass)

The task specification does not name the proof purpose of the carried credential; assertionMethod is the Data Integrity reading and VRC-ISS asserts it for relationship credentials. Not gating. (observed: pass)

The specification says the proof carries the verifier's nonce and domain; Data Integrity names the first member `challenge`, and where the verifier's nonce comes from (the query task) is outside this suite. The vector sends `challenge` and takes the nonce from the helper `presentationNonce`. Not gating. (observed: pass)
As CEX-011: the nonce member name and the nonce's source are not fixed by the specification. Not gating. (observed: pass)
As CEX-011: the audience is the proof's `domain` in the Data Integrity reading; the specification names it only as the audience. Not gating. (observed: pass)
Whether a nonce is single use is the verifier's policy; the specification says only that a nonce it no longer considers fresh is stale. Not gating. (observed: fail)
